newsitem.title: USA: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-ALABAMA BEATS MICHIGAN IN OUTBACK BOWL.
newsitem.headline: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-ALABAMA BEATS MICHIGAN IN OUTBACK BOWL.

text.p: Gene Stallings, whose seven years as Alabama head coach included a national title and an NCAA probation, left a winner Wednesday in his last game with a 17-14 victory over Michigan in the Outback Bowl.

"I can't tell you how pleased I am for the players," Stallings said. "I can't tell you how good a football game that was on both sides of the ball. Winning the last game is a lot easier because you don't have to appologize during the offseason. You can enjoy your summer more and it makes the transition a little easier."

Stallings announced his resignation, effective at the end of the season, following a 24-23 victory over Auburn on November 23rd. Alabama then lost to Florida in the Southeastern conference title game and improved to 10-3 with Wednesday's victory. Defensive coordinator Mike Dubose will replace Stallings.
Stallings, 61, was 70-15-1 at Alabama, where he was an assistant coach under the legendary Paul "Bear" Bryant from 1958-64.

After his stint as Bryant's assistant, Stallings returned to his alma mater, Texas A&M, where he went 27-45-1 in seven seasons as head coach. He moved to the professional, working as an assistant under Tom Landry with the Dallas Cowboys from 1972-85 before taking the head coaching job with the St. Louis Cardinals.
The Cardinals were 23-34-1 in four years with Stallings at the helm.

In Stallings' third year as Alabama's head coach, the Crimson Tide won the 1992 national championship with a 13-0 record, defeating Miami in the Sugar Bowl. Three of Stallings' first five Crimson Tide teams finished the regular season in the top five nationally, and Stallings guided Alabama to wins in bowls the last five seasons.

But shortly after Alabama's 1992 season, the school was placed on two years' probation that involved defensive back Antonio Langham's dealings with an agent in the hours following the Sugar Bowl victory.
